# Results — Study 192 (Tax-Day) on real ^GSPC daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The "tax-day effect":
two-sided test of whether US equity returns are elevated in the **10 trading days
before the April 15 federal filing deadline** (the "IRA contribution / refund flow"
claim) and in the **5 trading days on or after April 15** (the "post-deadline
normalisation" claim). Tested on ^GSPC daily close-to-close log-returns from
**1928-01-03 to 2026-06-12** (24,728 trading days, 99 years). Controls: (1) all
other trading days as the unconditional baseline, (2) the full month of April as a
broad seasonal baseline, (3) an October-15 placebo of identical window sizes. Two
hypotheses → Bonferroni k=2 correction applied. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC (shared `_cache/^GSPC_split_only.parquet`) | 1928-01-03 to 2026-06-12 | `df3897aef897` |

## Window definitions

The **effective tax deadline** is April 15, shifted to the next Monday when April 15
falls on a Saturday or Sunday. The calendar is deterministic (pure date arithmetic; no
hard-coded holiday table). Pre-tax and post-tax windows are mutually exclusive: the
deadline day itself is counted in the post-tax window only.

| Window | Trading days/yr | Total obs (99 yrs) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Pre-tax (10 days before deadline) | ~10 | 990 |
| Post-tax (5 days on/after deadline) | ~5 | 495 |
| October-15 placebo (same sizes) | ~15 | 1,480 |
| All April (broad seasonal) | ~21 | 2,049 |
| Unconditional all-day | ~252 | 24,728 |

## H1 — Pre-tax window vs rest

| Arm | n | mean (bps/day) | contrast (bps) | HAC t | Welch t | p-value | Bonf-p (k=2) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-tax window (10 days) | 990 | +7.77 | +5.55 | +1.865 | +1.452 | 0.1469 | **0.2937** |
| Rest (non-window days) | 23,738 | +2.22 | — | — | — | — | — |

The pre-tax window is slightly elevated (+5.55 bps/day above the rest), consistent with
the folk narrative (IRA contribution / refund inflows). However, the HAC t-stat is
**+1.865** and the Welch p = **0.1469** — well below the conventional significance
threshold and failing the Bonferroni bar at **0.2937**. The signal is not statistically
real.

## H2 — Post-tax window vs rest

| Arm | n | mean (bps/day) | contrast (bps) | HAC t | Welch t | p-value | Bonf-p (k=2) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Post-tax window (5 days) | 495 | +9.32 | +7.02 | +1.819 | +1.167 | 0.2437 | **0.4874** |
| Rest (non-window days) | 24,233 | +2.30 | — | — | — | — | — |

Similarly, the post-deadline window shows a higher-than-average mean (+9.32 bps) but the
contrast is noisy: Welch p = **0.2437**, Bonf-p = **0.4874**. With only 495 observations
the window is underpowered against any effect smaller than ~15-20 bps/day.

## Broad April seasonal baseline

| Arm | n | mean (bps/day) | contrast vs rest | p-value |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Full April | 2,049 | +5.68 | +3.53 | 0.1948 |
| Non-April days | 22,679 | +2.15 | — | — |
| Unconditional (all days) | 24,728 | +2.44 | — | — |

April as a whole is marginally above the annual mean (+3.53 bps/day contrast), but this
too is statistically indistinguishable from noise (p = 0.1948). The tax-window premium
cannot be separated from a weak, non-significant April seasonal.

## October-15 placebo

| Arm | n | mean (bps/day) | contrast vs rest | p-value |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Oct-15 window (same sizes) | 1,480 | +3.34 | +0.95 | 0.8244 |

The October-15 placebo windows — same sizes (10 pre + 5 post), no IRS event — produce
+3.34 bps/day (contrast +0.95, p = 0.82). The April tax windows (+7.77 bps pre, +9.32
bps post) are notably higher in point estimate, but given that:
  - The April numbers do not survive Bonferroni correction, and
  - The October placebo itself is positive (random draw), the

the gap between April and October is fully consistent with sampling variation.

## Multiple-comparisons summary

| Hypothesis | Raw p | Bonferroni p (k=2) | Survives? |
|---|--:|--:|:--|
| H1 — pre-tax window | 0.1469 | 0.2937 | No |
| H2 — post-tax window | 0.2437 | 0.4874 | No |

Neither hypothesis survives the Bonferroni correction. No result clears even the raw
5% threshold before correction.

## Could you trade it?

Approximately **10 pre-tax + 5 post-tax = 15 trading days per year** carry the signal.
The point-estimate premium is ~5-7 bps/day. To extract it as a long-only SPY position
you would: (a) hold SPY for 15 days/year, (b) hold cash otherwise. At even the lowest
realistic round-trip cost (~1 bp), the strategy loses money on the round-trip versus
simply holding SPY year-round (which earns the positive drift on all 252 days). The
"alpha" is a *pre-cost conditional premium vs the rest*, not a tradable excess return
versus a passive benchmark.

Even ignoring costs: with 99 yearly episodes the strategy's annual P&L variance is
enormous. The signal has not survived statistical inference, let alone cost and
implementation friction.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Both hypotheses fail the Bonferroni-corrected significance bar.
  The pre-tax window HAC t = +1.87 and post-tax HAC t = +1.82 are above the naive
  |t|=1.96 bar before correction but not after (Bonf-p 0.29 and 0.49). With only 10-5
  events per year over 99 years the study is underpowered against effects below
  ~15 bps/day. The point-estimate premium is consistent with the folk narrative but
  cannot be distinguished from noise with the power available.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A long-equity position in a 15-day window per year earns
  less than the market's unconditional drift. No cost-surviving excess return exists.
  ~10 annual events is insufficient frequency to bootstrap meaningful conviction.
- **April IRA inflow effect** — the broad April seasonal is also noise (p = 0.19);
  the window premium cannot be isolated from a weak April positive that itself fails
  significance.
